knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Gradient Vector Field of a Function

question.:question/problem: Find the gradient vector field of the function $f(x,y)=\sqrt{2 x - 1} - \sqrt{4 y + 1}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The gradient vector field of a function $f$ is given by $\nabla f.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}f_{x}(x,y)&=\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(\sqrt{2 x - 1} - \sqrt{4 y + 1}\right) \\ &=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2 x - 1}} \\ f_{y}(x,y)&=\frac{\partial}{\partial y}\left(\sqrt{2 x - 1} - \sqrt{4 y + 1}\right) \\ &=- \frac{2}{\sqrt{4 y + 1}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the gradient vector field of $f(x,y)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(x,y)&=f_{x}(x,y)\,i+f_{y}(x,y)\,j \\ &= \frac{1}{\sqrt{2 x - 1}}\,i- \frac{2}{\sqrt{4 y + 1}}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the gradient vector field of the function $f(x,y)=\ln{\left(2 x + 4 y \right)}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The gradient vector field of a function $f$ is given by $\nabla f.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}f_{x}(x,y)&=\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(\ln{\left(2 x + 4 y \right)}\right) \\ &=\frac{2}{2 x + 4 y} \\ f_{y}(x,y)&=\frac{\partial}{\partial y}\left(\ln{\left(2 x + 4 y \right)}\right) \\ &=\frac{4}{2 x + 4 y}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the gradient vector field of $f(x,y)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(x,y)&=f_{x}(x,y)\,i+f_{y}(x,y)\,j \\ &= \frac{2}{2 x + 4 y}\,i+\frac{4}{2 x + 4 y}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the gradient vector field of the function $f(x,y)=\tan{\left(x - 2 y \right)}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The gradient vector field of a function $f$ is given by $\nabla f.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}f_{x}(x,y)&=\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(\tan{\left(x - 2 y \right)}\right) \\ &=\sec^{2}{\left(x - 2 y \right)} \\ f_{y}(x,y)&=\frac{\partial}{\partial y}\left(\tan{\left(x - 2 y \right)}\right) \\ &=- 2 \sec^{2}{\left(x - 2 y \right)}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the gradient vector field of $f(x,y)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(x,y)&=f_{x}(x,y)\,i+f_{y}(x,y)\,j \\ &= \sec^{2}{\left(x - 2 y \right)}\,i- 2 \sec^{2}{\left(x - 2 y \right)}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}f_{x}(x,y,z)&=\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(x \ln{\left(- 2 y + z \right)}\right) \\ &=\ln{\left(- 2 y + z \right)} \\ f_{y}(x,y,z)&=\frac{\partial}{\partial y}\left(x \ln{\left(- 2 y + z \right)}\right) \\ &=- \frac{2 x}{- 2 y + z} \\ f_{z}(x,y,z)&=\frac{\partial}{\partial z}\left(x \ln{\left(- 2 y + z \right)}\right) \\ &=\frac{x}{- 2 y + z}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the gradient vector field of $f(x,y,z)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(x,y,z)&=f_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+f_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+f_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\ &= \ln{\left(- 2 y + z \right)}\,i- \frac{2 x}{- 2 y + z}\,j+\frac{x}{- 2 y + z}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the gradient vector field of the function $f(x,y,z)=\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2}}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The gradient vector field of a function $f$ is given by $\nabla f.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}f_{x}(x,y,z)&=\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2}}\right) \\ &=\frac{x}{\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2}}} \\ f_{y}(x,y,z)&=\frac{\partial}{\partial y}\left(\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2}}\right) \\ &=\frac{y}{\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2}}} \\ f_{z}(x,y,z)&=\frac{\partial}{\partial z}\left(\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2}}\right) \\ &=\frac{z}{\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2}}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the gradient vector field of $f(x,y,z)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(x,y,z)&=f_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+f_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+f_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\ &= \frac{x}{\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2}}}\,i+\frac{y}{\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2}}}\,j+\frac{z}{\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2}}}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the gradient vector field of the function $f(x,y,z)=\sin{\left(x z + 2 y \right)}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The gradient vector field of a function $f$ is given by $\nabla f.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}f_{x}(x,y,z)&=\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(\sin{\left(x z + 2 y \right)}\right) \\ &=z \cos{\left(x z + 2 y \right)} \\ f_{y}(x,y,z)&=\frac{\partial}{\partial y}\left(\sin{\left(x z + 2 y \right)}\right) \\ &=2 \cos{\left(x z + 2 y \right)} \\ f_{z}(x,y,z)&=\frac{\partial}{\partial z}\left(\sin{\left(x z + 2 y \right)}\right) \\ &=x \cos{\left(x z + 2 y \right)}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the gradient vector field of $f(x,y,z)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(x,y,z)&=f_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+f_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+f_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\ &= z \cos{\left(x z + 2 y \right)}\,i+2 \cos{\left(x z + 2 y \right)}\,j+x \cos{\left(x z + 2 y \right)}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the gradient vector field of the function $f(x,y,z)=\arctan{\left(x y z \right)}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The gradient vector field of a function $f$ is given by $\nabla f.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}f_{x}(x,y,z)&=\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(\arctan{\left(x y z \right)}\right) \\ &=\frac{y z}{x^{2} y^{2} z^{2} + 1} \\ f_{y}(x,y,z)&=\frac{\partial}{\partial y}\left(\arctan{\left(x y z \right)}\right) \\ &=\frac{x z}{x^{2} y^{2} z^{2} + 1} \\ f_{z}(x,y,z)&=\frac{\partial}{\partial z}\left(\arctan{\left(x y z \right)}\right) \\ &=\frac{x y}{x^{2} y^{2} z^{2} + 1}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the gradient vector field of $f(x,y,z)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(x,y,z)&=f_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+f_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+f_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\ &= \frac{y z}{x^{2} y^{2} z^{2} + 1}\,i+\frac{x z}{x^{2} y^{2} z^{2} + 1}\,j+\frac{x y}{x^{2} y^{2} z^{2} + 1}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: \frac{y z}{x y z + 1}\,i+\frac{z^{2}}{x y z + 1}\,j+\frac{x y}{x y z + 1}\,k

question.:question/problem: Find the gradient vector field of the function $f(x,y,z)=x^{2} z + x y^{3} - y z^{4}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The gradient vector field of a function $f$ is given by $\nabla f.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}f_{x}(x,y,z)&=\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(x^{2} z + x y^{3} - y z^{4}\right) \\ &=2 x z + y^{3} \\ f_{y}(x,y,z)&=\frac{\partial}{\partial y}\left(x^{2} z + x y^{3} - y z^{4}\right) \\ &=3 x y^{2} - z^{4} \\ f_{z}(x,y,z)&=\frac{\partial}{\partial z}\left(x^{2} z + x y^{3} - y z^{4}\right) \\ &=x^{2} - 4 y z^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the gradient vector field of $f(x,y,z)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(x,y,z)&=f_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+f_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+f_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\ &= \left(2 x z + y^{3}\right)\,i+\left(3 x y^{2} - z^{4}\right)\,j+\left(x^{2} - 4 y z^{3}\right)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$
